key_insight: The paper turns the Eshelby stability question into a quantitative geometry-vs-strain framework, linking interior strain heterogeneity to distance from an ellipsoid and to finite-shape residual-field bounds.
engineering_relevance: It gives engineers a way to assess how far an inclusion’s actual shape departs from ideal ellipsoidal behavior and how that affects local strain, supporting safer microstructure and defect design.
method: Derived a nonlinear two-sided stability relation for uniform dilatational eigenstrain in isotropic solids.
Used half-order Sobolev scaling to connect strain heterogeneity with a geometry-only measure of non-ellipsoidal shape.
Built a finite-shape residual-field budget via ellipsoidal subtraction to obtain convergent upper and lower bounds.
evidence_signal: The bounds were tested on protruded, indented, and necked inclusions and matched independent displacement-based finite-element calculations.
watch_item: The framework is strongest for the stated isotropic, uniform dilatational eigenstrain setting, so extending it to more complex material laws or loading modes will require extra validation.
paper_title: Quantitative Eshelby stability: local and finite-shape theory through AI-assisted mechanics
